title: Harman Kardon Citation MultiBeam 700 Compact Soundbar $189 + $50 Delivery ($0 NSW C&C) @ McCalls AV
body:
Deal: Harman Kardon Citation MultiBeam 700 Compact Soundbar $189 + $50 Delivery ($0 NSW C&C) @ McCalls AV

[Amolll] I grabbed one from the previous deal and have been using it since. Really happy with it and would definitely recommend it, especially at $189.
[Zio] Whats with the 3 months warranty whats wrong with them?
[Doyen] Free shipping over $111 deal doesn't seem to apply to Sydney WA or NT that i tried so far.
[Doyen] To ship it Sydney to Perth would be $24.95 standard post without commercial discount or $32.95 express post. Must cost them $25 to print a label and stick it on the box.
[drillvoice] I am comparing this with the JBL deal recently posted, mainly for watching movies and wanting clearer/better dialogue. The JBL apparently has a dedicated centre channel, but I may not get great use of that with a Bluetooth connection anyway. Whereas this has 3.5mm aux cable option. Any thoughts? Anyone want to help a brother out?
[Domingo] What device are you connecting it to? If it's a TV, HDMI would be more straightforward?
I have the JBL SB550 which is a 3 channel and find it much better for dialogue than my old Jamo 2.1 soundbar.
[donman92] Tempting for portability but I'll probably stick with my HT-S350 since it has Dolby Digital.
[yanman] "3-month warranty limit" is legally unenforceable if a product fails prematurely in Australia.
Under the Australian Consumer Law (ACL), all purchases from a business automatically come with statutory consumer guarantees that cannot be excluded, hidden, or limited by store policies.
[1] ( https://www.accc.gov.au/system/files/1449_ACL%20Motor%20vehi… ),
[2] ( https://www.becklegal.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Your… )
According to the Product Safety Australia platform, “All businesses, including those that sell online, must comply with consumer guarantees, including when they are selling second-hand products.”
Refurbished & Second-Hand Goods: The ACL explicitly covers refurbished and second-hand items sold by commercial businesses. The law states that a product must be of acceptable quality and durable enough to last for a "reasonable" timeframe based on its price point and original positioning.
A premium $799 home audio asset is legally expected to last much longer than 3 months, even if purchased on clearance.
